record_reviews.note: All seven versions preserve the chair movement. Japanese and Portuguese need the low sound relation clarified; the other five are acceptable.
The no-reply state, three readers and two-day interval match in all seven versions. Portuguese needs a grammatical read-status label.
The five-minute interval, empty exterior and missing lock are retained. Japanese and Spanish omit locking in the final clause, and Portuguese mistranslates the physical lock and door pronoun.
The seven versions preserve calming Yuna before the same locked-door aftermath. The same Japanese, Spanish and Portuguese issues apply; French also has a missing letter in calmer.
All seven versions preserve the speaker indicator, the gaze sliding toward the narrator and its disappearance. No change is necessary.
All seven versions preserve wipe marks, no graffiti and a surface one shade lighter. No change is necessary.
All seven versions preserve the alternating observation behind the narrator and in the mirror. Correct French location accents and Portuguese absence grammar while retaining the clipped sequence.
Six versions distinguish blood collection from connecting the IV. Japanese repeats the faulty shared connection predicate. French only needs accent corrections.
All seven versions retain stopping and the complete disappearance of both pursuit and stair sounds. Chinese retains the old-building location; the other six omit it.

All seven versions retain hiding, trembling breathing and the finger-to-lips gesture. Spanish and French omit the footsteps passing by. The Korean leaves the owner of the lips implicit, so the German specification is recorded as an ambiguity without an automatic correction.
